clue.text: Lovely skill of fielder on view

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing set on another comes after it, so the second part follows the first

blocks.note: to eye something is to view it
a cricket fielder's key skill is taking catches

explanation.surface: Admiring a cricket fielder's lovely catch made in full view of the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skill of fielder' reads as part of a description of fine play, but it is one piece placed after the verb for 'view'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking enough to grab your attention is attractive, so lovely things are often described this way.

clue.text: Formal sign-off terribly serious with NYC bank

indicators.note: something done terribly is done badly and out of order, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the anagram fodder
taken as written, also part of the fodder
to bank on someone is to rely on them

explanation.surface: A very solemn letter ending from a New York bank.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram takes in both SERIOUS and the letters NYC; 'bank' is a verb, as in bank on, not a building in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the conventional closing phrase written above your signature at the end of a polite letter to a named person.

clue.text: Animal snaring river bird

indicators.note: to snare is to trap and hold, so one piece is caught inside another

blocks.note: a cow is a farm animal
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A predator catching a waterbird by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The animal is only the outer shell; the bird at the end is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A crow is a common large black bird, so the general word names it fairly.

clue.text: Old king I entered in test, educational session

indicators.note: something that has entered is now inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: Tutankhamun, the ancient Egyptian king, is known as King Tut
taken as written
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch sits an exam, as if back at school.
explanation.walkthrough: The test here is ORAL, not TRIAL; I goes inside it and the old king stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a small teaching meeting with a tutor, so it is a lesson or period of instruction.

clue.text: Gas fire fixed for farm animal

indicators.note: something fixed has been repaired or rearranged, so these letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium
taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Repairing a gas heater in the farmhouse to keep the livestock warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas fire' reads as one domestic heater; split it into the gas symbol and a word to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young cow that has not yet calved, a kind of cattle kept on farms.

clue.text: Nothing present, nought ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: the present is now
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Nothing here at all, zero in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' is the time, not a gift or being in attendance. The answer is northern English dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: In the dialect of northern England this word is the everyday way of saying zilch, as in 'you get nowt for nowt'.

clue.text: Nicer PC, when aggravated, attacking lover

indicators.note: something aggravated is stirred up and disturbed, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder
attacking someone is harming them

explanation.surface: A police constable, normally pleasant, turns violent on someone's partner when provoked.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a police constable, but it is just two letters of fodder. The lover is the fairytale hero who wins Cinderella.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairytale hero is the ideal romantic suitor, and the name is used for any perfect boyfriend.

clue.text: Aggressive driver, alas a criminal

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked and wrong, so these letters are bent out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A road-rage motorist turns out, sadly, to be a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aggressive driver' reads as one phrase; only the first word defines, and the driver goes into the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An adversarial stance treats others as opponents, involving hostile confrontation rather than cooperation.

clue.text: Ace in space?

blocks.note: first meaning: superb, wonderful
second meaning, taken literally: beyond the Earth

explanation.surface: An astronaut's ace exploits up among the stars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' could suggest a pilot or a playing card; it is the slang adjective for excellent. The question mark flags that the second meaning is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom praises something as extraordinarily good, while literally it describes a place off the planet, among the stars.

clue.text: Play your way?

blocks.note: first meaning: a Shakespeare comedy
second meaning: however you prefer

explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' reads as a verb inviting you to play however you want; it is a noun, the title of a comedy by Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: The comedy set in the Forest of Arden is titled with a phrase that means according to your own preference.

clue.text: Really, really average!

blocks.note: so means very or really, as in 'so good'
the same again

explanation.surface: Someone stressing, with exclamation, how utterly ordinary something is.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word sounds like emphasis but gives the same two letters twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as so-so is neither good nor bad, merely middling or mediocre in quality.

clue.text: Ram I fed to god

indicators.note: food fed to someone goes inside them, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: Ares is the Greek god of war
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone offering a ram as a sacrifice to a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: The sacrifice picture hides a simple insertion of one letter into the Greek war god.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign and constellation is symbolised by the ram, which gives it its standard crossword sense.

clue.text: Cost warranted, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only part of the text is used

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: The price was partly justified.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the second to the fifth letter of the middle word.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the stake each player must put in before a hand, so it is the price of playing.

clue.text: Note minister gets if sent up

indicators.note: in a down answer, sending something up makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister of religion
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clergyman receives a note, perhaps a memo, if he is mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: A fiver is British slang for a five-pound note; 'Note' looks musical or written but means banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal word names the five-pound banknote, so it is a kind of paper money note.

clue.text: Nation, awful mess

blocks.note: first meaning: a country with its own government
second meaning: a dreadful condition of disorder, as when a room is in a shambles

explanation.surface: A cynical verdict that the country is in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a gripe about the country, the clue is two separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a sovereign country, and informally a dreadful condition of disorder, as in 'look at the state of this'.

clue.text: Go in lair, trembling first

indicators.note: something trembling is shaking, and shaken letters fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone nervously entering a beast's den, shaking, ahead of the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' sounds like an instruction about who goes in, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The original version of something is the earliest one, existing before any later copies or changes.

clue.text: Capital observed while touring at that time

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: as can mean while, as in 'as I was leaving'
then means at that time

explanation.surface: A city seen on a sightseeing trip back in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The tourist picture hides that the touring is done by a two-letter word wrapping round the time word.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the capital city of Greece, so it is one example of a national capital.

clue.text: Their rock almost breaking in wind

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter
breaking something smashes it apart, so the letters reassemble in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word without its last letter

explanation.surface: Their rock nearly crumbling in a strong gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like weather but is the definition: wind means empty, pompous talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind is idiomatic for empty boastful talk, hot air, which is how inflated persuasive speech is often dismissed.

clue.text: Tongue in booze, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: judging by sound means what is heard matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: liquor is alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A tongue dipped into a drink to taste it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is whimsical: a tongue is the thing that does the licking.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue is the organ used for lapping, so it is jokingly described as the body's lapper.

clue.text: PM, one formulating plan on time

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing placed on another follows it, so the second part comes after

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
to hatch a plan is to devise it

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister, someone devising a scheme to finish on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was British Prime Minister from 1979 to 1990; PM is short for Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher led the UK government, so she is an example of a holder of the Prime Minister's office.

clue.text: Place of worship bloke felt extremely lacking?

indicators.note: lacking its extremes means the outermost letters are dropped

blocks.note: a chap is a man, a bloke
the word with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A man at church who feels spiritually empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely lacking' reads as a feeling of deep want; it tells you to strip the ends from the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a small church or a room set aside for prayer, so it is a building for religious services.

clue.text: Sci-fi captain, one carried by three kings

indicators.note: something carried is held within the bearers, so one piece goes inside the others

blocks.note: K, R (rex) and K are all abbreviations for king
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A spaceship commander borne aloft like the Magi's gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three kings' suggests the Magi, but it supplies three one-letter king abbreviations. Captain James T. Kirk commands the Enterprise in Star Trek.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Kirk is the famous starship commander of the Star Trek television series and films.

clue.text: Pasty, sensation scoffed by you and I

indicators.note: food scoffed is gobbled down inside the eater, so one piece goes into another

blocks.note: you and I together are we
a hit is a sensation, a big success

explanation.surface: Two people wolfing down a sensational Cornish pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pasty' looks like the pastry, which fits the eating picture; it is the adjective meaning pale. A Cornish pasty is a British baked pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A pasty complexion is unhealthily pale, so the adjective means lacking colour, like a pale face.

clue.text: Broadcast a retro song

indicators.note: retro means looking backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A radio station playing an old-fashioned hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retro' reads as old-fashioned, describing the song; it signals that the letters go backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo vocal piece in an opera, so it is a particular kind of song.

clue.text: Each beginning on solo, clarinet and maybe fiddle

indicators.note: the beginning of each word means only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A musician starting with solo clarinet, and perhaps violin to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' looks like the violin in a band, but it is the definition: a fiddle is a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle in British slang is a dishonest scheme or fraud, which is what a con or swindle is.

clue.text: Old Peruvian driving endlessly?

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is removed

blocks.note: someone driving is in a car

explanation.surface: An ancient Andean wondering about someone forever on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' must be read as the phrase IN CAR before its last letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Incas ruled an empire centred on Peru before the Spanish conquest, so one was an early Peruvian.

clue.text: Caption or lines misspelt – as The Guardian?

indicators.note: a word misspelt has its letters wrongly ordered, so these are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A dig at The Guardian newspaper, famous for its typos and nicknamed the Grauniad.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T and the misprint joke point at the newspaper; the definition is simply acting as a guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means in the place of a parent, describing someone such as a teacher acting with parental responsibility.

clue.text: Coppers in minute put on new uniform?

blocks.note: minute, pronounced my-NEWT, means tiny
to change is to put on different clothes

explanation.surface: Police officers taking a moment to don fresh uniforms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' looks like police, which fits the uniform; it means copper coins, British pennies and twopences.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-value copper-coloured coins are loose cash of little worth, which is what the phrase names.
